players.product: silicon-photonics foundry services (PH18 SiPho platform) + SiGe drivers/TIAs

quarterly_data.signal: GUIDANCE AND THE UPDATED 2028 MODEL: CEO Russell Ellwanger guided Q3 2026 mid-range revenue to $520 million, an annualized revenue run rate of above $2 billion. CFO Oren Shirazi: the updated model targets $3.6 billion annual revenue ($760 million above the February model target, a 27% revenue increase); $1.63 billion annual gross profit, a 45% gross margin versus 39% in the prior model ($510 million higher, 67% incremental gross profit); $1.38 billion annual operating profit, a 38% operating margin versus 32% ($480 million higher, 63% incremental); and $1.2 billion annual net profit, a 33% net margin versus 26% in the prior model and 20% in Q2 2026 ($450 million higher, 59% incremental), 'reflecting our enhanced product mix'. The model now includes the Arai (former Fab 6) repurposing for 12-inch SiPho and assumes all fabs at 85% utilization after full installation and qualification of the $920 million capex, forward wafer selling prices, and costs and completion dates of tool, process and customer-product qualification; the CFO says the selling price per wafer is usually the biggest variable. CEO: operating expenses fall to approximately 7% of revenue, 30% lower than current levels, while the model includes an increase of R&D investment by over 40% against present levels; Tower expects to reach the model 'at a minimum by run rate, nominally in the full year, in 2028', and expects to update its long-term financial model within the first quarters of 2027, 'depending upon how it actually turns out on the final build-out of the factory'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 guide $520 million mid-range; 2028 model $3.6 billion revenue, $1.63 billion gross profit (45%), $1.38 billion operating profit (38%), $1.2 billion net profit (33%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 P&L AND BALANCE SHEET (CFO Oren Shirazi): Q2 revenue of $460 million compares with $414 million in Q1 2026 and $372 million in Q2 2025. Gross profit was a record $138 million (30% gross margin), up 72% from $80 million in Q2 2025; operating profit was $90 million, 2.26 times Q2 2025; net profit was $91 million (20% net margin), up 95% or $44 million from $47 million; EPS was $0.80 basic and $0.79 diluted versus $0.49 basic and $0.41 diluted a year earlier. At the end of June 2026 total assets were $3.8 billion ($1.6 billion net fixed assets, predominantly fab machinery, and $2 billion current assets), the current ratio about 4.9x and shareholders' equity a record $3.1 billion. The $290 million of prepayments received from SiPho customers in Q1 2026, mostly towards 2027 capacity reservations, are carried as short- and long-term customer advances and counted as cash from operating activities.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 gross profit $138 million; operating profit $90 million; net profit $91 million; EPS $0.79 diluted; shareholders' equity $3.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CAPEX PROGRAM AND UTILIZATION: CFO Oren Shirazi says the $920 million investment plan extends SiGe and SiPho capacity and capability across the eight-inch fabs in Israel, Newport Beach and Texas and the 12-inch Uozu fab in Japan, and is on track in purchase orders, technology and process qualification, equipment arrivals and ramp plans; approximately 50% was paid through Q2 2026 and the remaining 50% is expected to be paid during H2 2026 and full year 2027. CEO Russell Ellwanger on Q2 utilization during the capacity ramp: Fab 2, Fab 3 and Fab 9 (200mm) between 80% and 85%, Fab 5 in Japan at 75%. In the Q&A he said Tower continues to increase capacity in Newport Beach and San Antonio and still plans further capacity increases at both sites.
quarterly_data.figure: $920 million plan ~50% paid through Q2 2026, rest H2 2026 and 2027; Fabs 2/3/9 at 80%-85%, Fab 5 at 75%

quarterly_data.signal: JAPAN TRACKS AND SIPHO CAPACITY, Q&A DETAIL (CEO Russell Ellwanger): the Track 1 build-out is in the 2028 model at 85% utilization; almost 100% of Track 1 output will be silicon photonics, Phase I 'is focused very strong directly on SiPho expansion' and all of that growth is 'already spoken for', while added SiGe capacity is mainly in Phase II. Track 2's 4x figure includes the Fab 6 increment, Fab 6 being used predominantly 'as an epicenter and also for some specialty packaging tools'; the split is not announced, but the predominant portion of the 4x growth will be silicon photonics and the next biggest silicon germanium. No Track 2 capacity numbers yet: Tower is in final negotiations on the timing to complete and facilitize the facility and with the equipment suppliers; budgets are approved, but the tool installation and qualification schedule and parts of the building plan are not final. He would say that after 2027 / mid-2028 all of the SiGe and SiPho growth, 'and definitely in SiPho', will be in 300mm. Track 2 is meant to support pluggables, NPO and 'the additional future market for co-package optics'. The Q4 2026 SiPho start rate of three times Q2 shipments is capacity, not bookings (CFO Oren Shirazi: the $1.3 billion is on customer committed contracts); CEO: 'the capacity growth is spoken for. Is it all booked? No, but it's spoken for', and no update to the contracts and bookings was given.
quarterly_data.figure: Track 2 4x Japan 300mm capacity includes Fab 6; Track 1 almost 100% silicon photonics

quarterly_data.signal: NON-OPTICAL BUSINESSES (CEO Russell Ellwanger): RF mobile was 12% of Q2 revenue. The RF SOI transition from 200mm to 300mm and the consolidation of 300mm RF SOI manufacturing resulted in a 14% year-over-year decrease in 300mm RF SOI revenue, but very strong 300mm design-win momentum, particularly for premium smartphones, drives an expected 3x increase in RF SOI 300mm wafer starts by mid-2027 against Q2 2026 shipments; he expects Q2-Q3 2027 to bring the largest 300mm RF SOI manufacturing Tower has ever done, with the Fab 10 factory 'very full come second, third quarter of next year'. Power management was 14% of Q2 revenue with year-over-year growth and strong demand for 200mm and 300mm BCD; Tower claims a leadership position in low gate charge and low RDSON LDMOS devices for high-performance-computing power delivery and saw increased demand from existing customers and very strong new customer acquisitions. Sensor/display was 12%: image-sensor revenue was predominantly flat year over year, but demand is surging for high-end machine-vision sensors used in semiconductor inspection and for EV battery inspection, expected to continue to grow over the next two years, served by the 300mm global shutter platform.
quarterly_data.figure: RF mobile 12%, power management 14%, sensor/display 12% of Q2 revenue; expected 3x 300mm RF SOI wafer starts by mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: COMPETITION AND SUPPLY (CEO Russell Ellwanger, Q&A): asked about capacity additions by GlobalFoundries, STMicro and Samsung, he said 'Supply's certainly increasing' but Tower is qualified at the lead customers worldwide with very strong contracts lasting through 2028 and is in strong discussions 'to maintain contracts well beyond that'; its focus is 'how we maintain sole share or majority share of our lead customers', and it believes market share with lead customers 'will stay extremely high', helped by programs for generation plus two and in many cases plus three. Tower differentiates in figure of merit, insertion loss being 'probably one of the biggest things', which lets integrators buy fewer and less expensive CW lasers. On Tower's own supply chain: 'Big picture, no' shortages - 'we're in very good shape on supply' for starting and variable materials.

connects_to.relationship: multi-year Indium Phosphide epiwafer supply agreement

contracts.signal: Tower CEO Russell Ellwanger: in support of heterogeneous III-V integration on silicon photonics (integrated lasers, advanced modulators), 'we enter into a multi-year epitaxial wafer supply agreement with IQE, securing a strategic supply of III-V epitaxial material'; on supply, 'We were under somewhat of a crunch for indium phosphide starting material, we believe that we've addressed that very nicely with the contract with IQE.'
